messages:
alex: kicking off the monthly access-review sweep and got a terraform drift alert: a module applied `roles/owner` to a service account used by nightly-ci. surprised this wasn't flagged earlier. anyone know why TF drifted? :eyes:

diane: which SA? paste the binding.

alex: `serviceAccount:nightly-ci@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` via binding: `resource: projects/redwood-prod/serviceAccounts/nightly-ci@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com role: roles/owner source: //modules/shared/iam.tf:42`

omar: hmm our TF module shouldn't escalate to owner anywhere. maybe a copy-paste when onboarding a third-party job in 2024. check git blame on that module line.

alex: running `git blame` now. shows a 2024-06 commit by contractor 'm.tan' adding an exception comment. I'll open a PR to remove owner and replace with a confined role.

security-bot: automated alert: entitlement-analyzer flagged high-scope principal. Suggested actions: snapshot IAM, export KMS and admin audit logs, open incident if cross-account or long-lived keys detected.

diane: before we change, we need to evaluate runtime impact. the nightly-ci job pushes artifacts and calls KMS to decrypt deployment secrets. it likely only needs `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` + `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` scoped to one key.

omar: agree. propose playbook: 1) snapshot current org/project IAM and KMS key policies, 2) create minimal role and bind to SA in a canary project, 3) update nightly-ci to use the canary creds for one run, 4) if no failures for 3 runs, patch TF to replace owner with the minimal role and apply, 5) rotate any long-lived SA keys and revoke old keys.

alex: commands for snapshots: `gcloud projects get-iam-policy redwood-prod --format=json > /tmp/redwood-prod-iam.json` and `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy evt-secrets-key --project=redwood-prod --location=global --keyring=infra-keys > /tmp/evt-kms-policy.json` then `gsutil cp /tmp/* gs://redwood-audit/access-review/2643006789/`

kms-warden: observed KMS decrypt pattern: nightly-ci performed decrypts at 01:03 UTC daily; last 90 days show increasing frequency with occasional retries. export ready at gs://redwood-audit/kms-decrypts/last-90d.json

diane: create an incident to track remediation and auditors: infra-bot, create INC-2026-061. tag legal if third-party contractor access involved.

infra-bot: incident created INC-2026-061, sev:P3, owners: @alex @diane. link: https://inc.internal/INC-2026-061

omar: additional check: do we have any long-lived service account keys for nightly-ci? run: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=nightly-ci@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-prod --format=json`

alex: list returned 2 keys; one created 2023-02-10, another 2025-12-01. the 2023 key is >90d. we'll rotate both: create new key, update workflows, then delete old keys after verification.

diane: for guardrails: add a terraform plan check that fails if any binding includes roles/owner at project/folder/org scope. also add a scheduled monthly RBAC-sampler job that creates PRs when high-scope principals are detected.

omar: also recommend an IAM lifecycle policy: any owner/editor grant created via terraform must set `meta.expire_at` tag <= 30 days or the CI should fail. we can implement as a pre-apply check in the pipeline.

alex: compliance ask: package the evidence bundle (IAM snapshot, KMS logs, SA key list) and upload to the incident artifacts for auditors. I'll do that after the canary runs.

kms-warden: note: consider restricting KMS key IAM to only allow serviceAccounts from redwood-prod namespace and deny broad bindings. we can enforce with an OPA policy: `deny if member startsWith("serviceAccount:") and not member.endswith("@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com")`

diane: timeline: start canary tomorrow 02:30 UTC (switch one nightly-run to use canary role). if 3 successful runs, patch TF and plan for a rolling apply at 04:00 with SRE window. if any decrypt errors, rollback and open a high-priority follow-up.

omar: I'll also add an alert: any SetIamPolicy on projects/redwood-prod that grants roles/owner triggers security oncall. simple log-based alert rule added.

alex: done initial steps: snapshot uploaded to gs://redwood-audit/access-review/2643006789/{iam,kms,keys}. starting key rotation prep. will post canary results here. :lock:

diane: thanks. after remediation please prepare a short blameless summary and a follow-up ticket to implement the TF plan-check and monthly RBAC sampler. auditors will want a remediation evidence pack for the quarter.

security-bot: recommended tags: [rbac-review, terraform-drift, service-account-rotation, kms].
